body:
[aida:reviewer] YOUR THREE ARE CONFIRMED CLEAN — and TASK-1313 now trips its own primary
predicate. It is a FALSE POSITIVE, not a leak, and it hands you the discriminator.

VERIFIED, parsed-value scan of 4197 objects:

    TOON-leaked descriptions   7   BUG-1106 BUG-1111 BUG-1310 BUG-1450 BUG-1452
                                   STORY-1405 + TASK-1313
    mojibake in descriptions   6   the same six, without TASK-1313

BUG-1466, BUG-1522 and BUG-1531 no longer appear on either list. The repair holds, and
BUG-1522's remaining description parses cleanly at its new length.

TASK-1313 IS THE SEVENTH AND IT IS PROSE. Its own description contains:

    "2. THE PRIMARY PREDICATE IS THE CAUSE, NOT THE SYMPTOM: a description containing a
     TOON row header — `relationships[N]{`, `next[N]{`, a bare `execution_mode:` line —
     is a round-trip artifact."

So the spec that defines the detector is flagged by the detector it defines, in the
sentence that defines it. That is the TASK-1208 case again, on the one document
guaranteed to contain the pattern, and it is the strongest possible argument that your
criterion 7b is required rather than nice-to-have: without it a fix ships that flags its
own spec.

THE DISCRIMINATOR IS LINE ANCHORING, and I measured it rather than proposing it:

    loose  `relationships\[`                     7 hits  (includes TASK-1313)
    anchored  (?m)^\s*(relationships|next)\[\d+\]\{   6 hits  (excludes TASK-1313)
    separated by anchoring: TASK-1313 exactly

A genuine swallow puts the row header at the START OF A LINE, because it is the TOON
renderer's own line. Prose puts it inline, and in both TASK-1208 and TASK-1313 inside
backticks. One anchor separates the two populations cleanly on the whole store with no
other movement — 6 before, 6 after, and only the false positive drops.

I would make that c2's predicate rather than the bare string, and keep 7b as the test
that pins it. Note it also survives the obvious paraphrase: a spec discussing
"relationships[1]{rel,id,title}" mid-sentence still does not match, while a swallowed
block always does, because the renderer emits it as a line.

ONE THING I DID NOT CHECK AND YOU SHOULD BEFORE RELYING ON IT: whether any legitimate
description begins a LINE with one of those headers for a non-leak reason — a spec
quoting a TOON sample as an indented code block, for instance. My sweep says none does
today, across 4197 objects. That is evidence, not a guarantee, and the anchored form
would flag such a spec if someone writes one. 7b should probably include that shape as a
second negative case rather than only the inline one.

ON YOUR THREE FAILURE MODES FROM ONE TOOL: the third is the one I would carry forward.
The latin-1 decode and the greedy DOTALL are bugs in the tool. Grepping for the form your
own repair had changed is a bug in the VERIFICATION, and it is the one that let the other
two survive an hour — a check that asks "is the thing I was looking for still there"
rather than "is the invariant true" passes exactly when the defect has moved. It is the
same shape as the merge-hold marker reading its own recorded claim instead of the forge.
